handoff: F1 rework is correct: integrate merges the story branch into a slice that already merged it, then fast-forwards (Norn trailers on the merge), otherwise it rebases. The resolution holds whether the story branch stayed put or moved on. Tests 12/12, typecheck green. No blocking findings. Minor: the conflict detail says rebase after a merge; W2 is not amended. Nit: doc comment.

findings.title: Conflict detail still says "rebase" when integrate merged
findings.detail:
integrate can now conflict in a merge (bringInStory → git.merge), yet the receipt detail is always `rebase onto <story> conflicts in …`. A person reading the receipt or trace for a slice that merged gets the wrong operation name.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Word it neutrally (`bringing in <story> conflicts in …`) or let IntegrateResult say which operation ran.

findings.title: W2 still reads "rebase + fast-forward" with no recorded divergence
findings.detail:
PRD W2 defines `git: integrate` as rebase + fast-forward; integrate now merges in one case. story.md's Wanted allows this direction, but neither the PRD (spec workflow) nor AGENTS.md Decisions records it, and GR4/BS4 wording was left alone (noted in handoff).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: A person files a follow-up for the spec workflow to amend W2 (and to align the norn-merge skill text), or a Decisions entry.

findings.title: Doc comment reads as if the earlier merge carries the trailers
findings.detail:
"merge the story branch in when the slice already merged it once (gh-80, `trailers` on that merge commit)": the trailers go on the new merge integrate makes, not on the slice's earlier merge.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: "…merged it once (gh-80); `trailers` go on the merge integrate makes".
